I need to trace how a browser request for another user's profile image (avatar) is served in this codebase — from the HTTP route handler all the way down to stored data. This is likely a web application. Search very thoroughly for:

1. Routes or handlers related to "avatar" or "profile image" or "user image" — look for URL patterns like `/avatar`, `/users/:id/avatar`, `/profile/image`, etc.
2. The handler function that serves avatar/profile images
3. Any service or middleware layer it calls
4. The data/storage layer it ultimately reads from

Search breadth: very thorough. Look in route definitions, controllers, handlers, services, repositories, and storage layers. Check for terms like "avatar", "profile_image", "user_image", "photo", "picture" in route files, handler files, and API definitions.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

29	const shutdownTimeout = 10 * time.Second
30	
31	type Server struct {
32		Secret  string
33		Profile *profile.Profile
34		Store   *store.Store
35	
36		echoServer *echo.Echo
37		httpServer *http.Server
38		sseHub     *apiv1.SSEHub
39	
40		backgroundRunnerCancels []context.CancelFunc
41		backgroundRunnerWG      sync.WaitGroup
42	}

44	func NewServer(ctx context.Context, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) (*Server, error) {
45		s := &Server{
46			Store:   store,
47			Profile: profile,
48		}
49	
50		echoServer := echo.New()
51		echoServer.Use(middleware.Recover())
52		echoServer.Use(newCORSMiddleware(profile))
53		s.echoServer = echoServer
54	
55		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
58		}
59	
60		secret := "usememos"
61		if !profile.Demo {
62			secret = instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey
63		}
64		s.Secret = secret
65	
66		// Register healthz endpoint.
67		echoServer.GET("/healthz", func(c *echo.Context) error {
68			return c.String(http.StatusOK, "Service ready.")
69		})

72		frontend.NewFrontendService(profile, store).Serve(ctx, echoServer)
73	
74		rootGroup := echoServer.Group("")
75	
76		apiV1Service := apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)
77		s.sseHub = apiV1Service.SSEHub
78	
79		// Register HTTP file server routes BEFORE gRPC-Gateway to ensure proper range request handling for Safari.
80		// This uses native HTTP serving (http.ServeContent) instead of gRPC for video/audio files.
81		fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret)
82		fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)

85		rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService).RegisterRoutes(rootGroup)
86	
87		// Register gRPC gateway as api v1 (includes SSE endpoint on CORS-enabled group).
88		if err := apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(ctx, echoServer); err != nil {
89			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register gRPC gateway")
90		}

92		mcpService, err := mcp.NewMCPService(profile, echoServer)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create MCP service")
95		}
96		mcpService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
97	
98		return s, nil

101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {
107			address = s.Profile.UNIXSock
108			network = "unix"
109		}
110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}
114	
115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}
121	
122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {
125			if err := s.httpServer.Serve(listener); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
126				slog.Error("failed to start echo server", "error", err)
127			}
128		}()
129		s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)
130	
131		return nil
132	}
133	
134	func (s *Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) {
135		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, shutdownTimeout)
136		defer cancel()
137	
138		slog.Info("server shutting down")
139	
140		s.stopBackgroundRunners()
141		s.closeLongLivedConnections()
142		s.shutdownHTTPServer(ctx)
143		s.waitBackgroundRunners(ctx)
144	
145		// Close database connection.
146		if err := s.Store.Close(); err != nil {
147			slog.Error("failed to close database", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
148		}
149	
150		slog.Info("memos stopped properly")
151	}
152	
153	func (s *Server) startBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
154		// Create a separate context for each background runner
155		// This allows us to control cancellation for each runner independently
156		s3Context, s3Cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
157	
158		// Store the cancel function so we can properly shut down runners
159		s.backgroundRunnerCancels = append(s.backgroundRunnerCancels, s3Cancel)
160	
161		// Create and start S3 presign runner
162		s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)
163		s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)
164	
165		// Start continuous S3 presign runner
166		s.backgroundRunnerWG.Add(1)
167		go func() {
168			defer s.backgroundRunnerWG.Done()
169			s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)
170			slog.Info("s3presign runner stopped")
171		}()
172	
173		slog.Info("background runners started")
174	}
175	
176	func (s *Server) stopBackgroundRunners() {
177		for _, cancelFunc := range s.backgroundRunnerCancels {
178			if cancelFunc != nil {
179				cancelFunc()
180			}
181		}
182	}
183	
184	func (s *Server) waitBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
185		done := make(chan struct{})
186		go func() {
187			s.backgroundRunnerWG.Wait()
188			close(done)
189		}()
190	
191		select {
192		case <-done:
193		case <-ctx.Done():
194			select {
195			case <-done:
196				return
197			default:
198			}
199			slog.Error("failed to stop background runners", slog.String("error", ctx.Err().Error()))
200		}
201	}
202	
203	func (s *Server) closeLongLivedConnections() {
204		// Long-lived SSE requests do not finish on their own during http.Server.Shutdown.
205		if s.sseHub != nil {
206			s.sseHub.Close()
207		}
208	}
209	
210	func (s *Server) shutdownHTTPServer(ctx context.Context) {
211		if s.httpServer == nil {
212			return
213		}
214		if err := s.httpServer.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
215			slog.Error("failed to shutdown server", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
216			if closeErr := s.httpServer.Close(); closeErr != nil && closeErr != http.ErrServerClosed {
217				slog.Error("failed to close server", slog.String("error", closeErr.Error()))
218			}
219		}
220	}
221	
222	func (s *Server) getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx context.Context) (*storepb.InstanceBasicSetting, error) {
223		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.Store.GetInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
224		if err != nil {
225			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
226		}
227		modified := false
228		if instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey == "" {
229			instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey = uuid.NewString()
230			modified = true
231		}
232		if modified {
233			instanceSetting, err := s.Store.UpsertInstanceSetting(ctx, &storepb.InstanceSetting{
234				Key:   storepb.InstanceSettingKey_BASIC,
235				Value: &storepb.InstanceSetting_BasicSetting{BasicSetting: instanceBasicSetting},
236			})
237			if err != nil {
238				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to upsert instance setting")
239			}
240			instanceBasicSetting = instanceSetting.GetBasicSetting()
241		}
242		return instanceBasicSetting, nil
243	}

14	// Profile is the configuration to start main server.
15	type Profile struct {
16		// Demo indicates if the server is in demo mode
17		Demo bool
18		// Addr is the binding address for server
19		Addr string
20		// Port is the binding port for server
21		Port int
22		// UNIXSock is the IPC binding path. Overrides Addr and Port
23		UNIXSock string
24		// Data is the data directory
25		Data string
26		// DSN points to where memos stores its own data
27		DSN string

30		Driver string

39	// AllowAnonymous reports whether unauthenticated visitors may access the instance.
40	//
41	// Anonymous access is enabled only when an InstanceURL is configured. An instance
42	// with no InstanceURL set is treated as private: anonymous callers are limited to
43	// the auth-bootstrap endpoints (sign-in, share links, etc.) and the web UI redirects
44	// them to the sign-in page instead of the public Explore view. Authenticated callers
45	// (session, access token, or personal access token) are never affected.
46	func (p *Profile) AllowAnonymous() bool {
47		return strings.TrimSpace(p.InstanceURL) != ""
48	}

50	func checkDataDir(dataDir string) (string, error) {
51		// Convert to absolute path if relative path is supplied.
52		if !filepath.IsAbs(dataDir) {
53			// Use current working directory, not the binary's directory
54			// This ensures we use the actual working directory where the process runs
55			absDir, err := filepath.Abs(dataDir)
56			if err != nil {
57				return "", err
58			}
59			dataDir = absDir
60		}
61	
62		// Trim trailing \ or / in case user supplies
63		dataDir = strings.TrimRight(dataDir, "\\/")
64		if _, err := os.Stat(dataDir); err != nil {
65			return "", errors.Wrapf(err, "unable to access data folder %s", dataDir)
66		}
67		return dataDir, nil
68	}
69	
70	func (p *Profile) Validate() error {
71		// Set default data directory if not specified
72		if p.Data == "" {
73			if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
74				p.Data = filepath.Join(os.Getenv("ProgramData"), "memos")
75			} else {
76				// On Linux/macOS, check if /var/opt/memos exists and is writable (Docker scenario)
77				if info, err := os.Stat("/var/opt/memos"); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
78					// Check if we can write to this directory
79					testFile := filepath.Join("/var/opt/memos", ".write-test")
80					if err := os.WriteFile(testFile, []byte("test"), 0600); err == nil {
81						os.Remove(testFile)
82						p.Data = "/var/opt/memos"
83					} else {
84						// /var/opt/memos exists but is not writable, use current directory
85						slog.Warn("/var/opt/memos is not writable, using current directory")
86						p.Data = "."
87					}
88				} else {
89					// /var/opt/memos doesn't exist, use current directory (local development)
90					p.Data = "."
91				}
92			}
93		}
94	
95		// Create data directory if it doesn't exist
96		if _, err := os.Stat(p.Data); os.IsNotExist(err) {
97			if err := os.MkdirAll(p.Data, 0770); err != nil {
98				slog.Error("failed to create data directory", slog.String("data", p.Data), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
99				return err
100			}
101		}
102	
103		dataDir, err := checkDataDir(p.Data)

Here is the full analysis. --- ## Complete Avatar Request Trace: From Browser to Stored Data This is a Go web application called **Memos** (github.com/usememos/memos), using the **Echo** HTTP framework for file serving and **gRPC-Gateway** for its API layer. The avatar data is stored as a **base64-encoded data URI** directly in the `avatar_url` column of the `user` database table. ### 1. Route Registration **File:** `/bench/repo/server/server.go` (lines 80-82) During server startup, `NewServer` creates a `FileServerService` and registers its routes on the Echo HTTP server: ```go fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret) fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer) ``` **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 121-125) `RegisterRoutes` registers the avatar endpoint at `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`: ```go func (s *FileServerService) RegisterRoutes(echoServer *echo.Echo) { fileGroup := echoServer.Group("/file") fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar) } ``` The endpoint is also listed as a **public method** (no authentication required on open instances) in the ACL config: **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` (line 25) ```go "/memos.api.v1.UserService/GetUserAvatar": {}, ``` ### 2. The Handler Function **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 167-209) The `serveUserAvatar` method is the HTTP handler. Its logic proceeds as follows: **Step A -- Private instance authentication check (lines 173-181):** If the instance is private (no `InstanceURL` configured, meaning `Profile.AllowAnonymous()` returns false), the handler requires authentication. It calls `s.getCurrentUser()` which delegates to `Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser()`. If no valid session/token is found, it returns 401 Unauthorized. **Step B -- Look up the user by username (lines 183-191):** Extracts the `:identifier` path parameter and calls `s.getUserByUsername(ctx, identifier)` which calls: ```go s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier}) ``` **Step C -- Check avatar existence (lines 192-194):** If the user's `AvatarURL` field is empty, returns 404 "avatar not found". **Step D -- Parse the data URI (lines 196-199):** Calls `s.parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL)` which uses the regex `^data:(?P[^;]+);base64,(?P.+)` to extract the MIME type and base64-decode the image data. **Step E -- Validate MIME type (lines 201-203):** Checks the parsed MIME type against `avatarAllowedTypes` (line 75): `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/jpg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, `image/heic`, `image/heif`. **Step F -- Serve the response (lines 205-209):** Sets security headers (`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, CSP), sets `Content-Type` to the image MIME type, sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`, and returns the decoded binary data as a blob. ### 3. Authentication / Middleware Layer **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 708-711) `getCurrentUser` extracts the `Authorization` header and `Cookie` header and delegates to the shared `Authenticator`: ```go func (s *FileServerService) getCurrentUser(ctx context.Context, c *echo.Context) (*store.User, error) { authHeader := c.Request().Header.Get(echo.HeaderAuthorization) cookieHeader := c.Request().Header.Get("Cookie") return s.authenticator.AuthenticateToUser(ctx, authHeader, cookieHeader) } ``` **File:** `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go` (lines 190-208) `AuthenticateToUser` tries three credential types in priority order: 1. **Access Token V2** (short-lived JWT from `Authorization: Bearer `) -- stateless validation 2. **Personal Access Token (PAT)** (from `Authorization: Bearer memos_pat_...`) -- validated against the database 3. **Refresh token cookie** (fallback for browser `` tags that cannot set Authorization headers) ### 4. The Store (Service) Layer **File:** `/bench/repo/store/user.go` (lines 148-169) `Store.GetUser` first checks an in-memory cache (keyed by user ID). Since the avatar lookup is by *username* (not ID), the cache is bypassed, and it delegates to `Store.ListUsers`: ```go func (s *Store) GetUser(ctx context.Context, find *FindUser) (*User, error) { // Cache check by ID (skipped for username lookups) list, err := s.ListUsers(ctx, find) // ... user := list[0] s.userCache.Set(ctx, userCacheKey(user.ID), user) return user, nil } ``` `ListUsers` calls `s.driver.ListUsers(ctx, find)` which dispatches to the database-specific driver. The `User` struct (lines 29-45) contains the `AvatarURL` field: ```go type User struct { ID int32 RowStatus RowStatus CreatedTs int64 UpdatedTs int64 Username string Role Role Email string Nickname string PasswordHash string AvatarURL string Description string } ``` ### 5. The Database Layer **File:** `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go` (lines 88-205) The SQLite driver's `ListUsers` builds a query selecting from the `user` table. When the `FindUser` has `Username` set, it adds `WHERE username = ?`. The `avatar_url` column is selected and scanned into `user.AvatarURL` (line 189): ```sql SELECT id, username, role, email, nickname, password_hash, avatar_url, description, created_ts, updated_ts, row_status FROM user WHERE username = ? ``` Equivalent implementations exist for: - **PostgreSQL:** `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user.go` (line 150 selects `avatar_url`, line 179 scans it) - **MySQL:** `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user.go` (line 147 selects `avatar_url`, line 170 scans it) ### 6. Schema / Data Format **File:** `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` (line 20) ```sql avatar_url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', ``` The avatar is stored as a **data URI** directly in the database column, e.g.: ``` data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo... ``` This was confirmed by the test helper at `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go` (lines 443-451). ### 7. How the Frontend Gets the Avatar URL **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` (lines 16-41) When the API returns a `User` protobuf to the frontend, `convertUserFromStore` replaces base64 data URIs with a pointer URL to avoid sending large blobs in API responses: ```go if user.AvatarURL != "" { _, _, err := extractImageInfo(user.AvatarURL) if err == nil { userpb.AvatarUrl = fmt.Sprintf("/file/%s/avatar", userpb.Name) } else { userpb.AvatarUrl = user.AvatarURL // external URL, pass through } } ``` Here `userpb.Name` is the resource name like `users/steven`, so the resulting URL is `/file/users/steven/avatar`. If the `AvatarURL` is an external URL (not a data URI), it is passed through directly. **File:** `/bench/repo/web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx` The frontend `UserAvatar` component renders a simple `` tag pointing to whatever `avatarUrl` the API returned (either `/file/users//avatar` or an external URL). ### Summary: Complete Request Flow ``` Browser | v Echo router: GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar | v fileserver.serveUserAvatar(c) [fileserver.go:167] | +-- (private instance?) getCurrentUser() [fileserver.go:173] | | | v | Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser() [authenticator.go:190] | (checks Bearer token, then cookie) | +-- getUserByUsername(ctx, "steven") [fileserver.go:715] | | | v | Store.GetUser(&FindUser{Username: "steven"}) [user.go:148] | | | v | Store.ListUsers() [user.go:136] | | | v | driver.ListUsers() (sqlite/postgres/mysql) | | | v | SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ? | | | v | store.User{AvatarURL: "data:image/png;base64,iVBOR..."} | +-- parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL) [fileserver.go:737] | extracts MIME type + base64-decodes to []byte | +-- validate avatarAllowedTypes [fileserver.go:75] | +-- c.Blob(200, "image/png", imageData) [fileserver.go:209] sets Content-Type, Cache-Control, security headers ``` ### Key Files (all absolute paths) | Layer | File | |-------|------| | Server startup / route wiring | `/bench/repo/server/server.go` | | Route registration + HTTP handler | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` | | Handler tests | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go` | | Authentication logic | `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go` | | Public endpoints ACL | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` | | API user converter (URL rewriting) | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` | | User update (avatar validation) | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go` | | Store layer (User struct + caching) | `/bench/repo/store/user.go` | | Store interface (Driver) | `/bench/repo/store/driver.go` | | SQLite driver | `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go` | | PostgreSQL driver | `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user.go` | | MySQL driver | `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user.go` | | DB schema (SQLite) | `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` | | Profile (AllowAnonymous) | `/bench/repo/internal/profile/profile.go` | | Frontend avatar component | `/bench/repo/web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx` | | Protobuf definition | `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto` |
